claims.text: A conventional low-alloy tempered martensitic steel susceptible to temper embrittlement can manifest a ductile-brittle-ductile transition.
Temper embrittlement in this steel arises from impurities segregating to grain boundaries within a narrow temperature window.
A controlled temperature cycle spanning temperatures below, within, and above the embrittlement range will produce the proposed transition.
The steel is ductile at a temperature below the embrittlement window.
Impurity segregation embrittles the steel in an intermediate temperature window.
The steel's ductility is restored at temperatures above the embrittlement window.
Heat treatment and tempering produce grain-boundary impurity segregation in the steel.
At intermediate temperature, impurities migrate to and segregate at grain boundaries.
Grain-boundary impurity segregation weakens the grain boundaries.
Weakened grain boundaries induce brittle fracture.
Below the critical temperature window, reduced impurity diffusion restores ductile behavior.
Above the critical temperature window, redistribution of impurities restores ductile behavior.
The material will lose substantial ductility and tend toward brittle fracture only in the narrow intermediate temperature window.
The as-tempered steel has uniform ductility under ambient conditions.
The proposed behavior is restricted to conventional alloys susceptible to temper embrittlement.
Compositionally complex and high-entropy alloys do not exhibit the impurity-driven grain-boundary segregation effects described here.
Compositionally complex and high-entropy alloys will not exhibit this ductile-brittle-ductile transition.

contradictions.description: The structural mediator is described as segregation already produced by heat treatment and tempering, while the mechanism treats segregation as developing during intermediate-temperature testing. The experiment varies test temperature but does not specify tempering temperature, hold time, or cooling history needed to distinguish pre-existing segregation from segregation produced during testing.

The mediator posits existing grain-boundary segregation, whereas the mechanism says reduced diffusion below the window restores ductility. Reduced diffusion could inhibit new segregation but, by itself, does not remove segregation already established by heat treatment.
